data.narrative:
Sunfire is a Series E climate and energy technology company founded by Carl Berninghausen, Nils Aldag, and Christian von Olshausen, having raised $315M+ to date. The comparable universe consists of one public company (LNZA) and eight private-sector peers including Redwood Materials, QuantumScape, KoBold Metals, Electric Hydrogen, and Enovix.

A stage-progression valuation method applies a 1.4x multiplier to the $315M total raised proxy, reflecting typical step-ups from Series E to the next funding stage, yielding $441M. A peer-median approach proved inapplicable: while eight same-sector peers exist in Climate & Energy, insufficient clustering emerged within narrow filters (zero same-stage matches, one adjacent-stage match, zero similar-tier matches), falling short of the three-datapoint threshold required for reliable median construction.

The analysis supports a valuation range of $375M to $507M, centered on $441M. This single-method triangulation carries material execution risk: the lack of closely-matched peer comparables limits external validation of the stage-progression step-up. Key uncertainties include actual deployment progress relative to competitors in hydrogen and energy storage, capital intensity of commercialization, and whether the 1.4x multiplier reflects Sunfire's risk profile relative to the broader Climate & Energy cohort. Additional market data on recent Series E–F financings in the sector would improve confidence in the implied range.
